task: Replace the no-body MCP server clone with a backend form-based clone flow (clone_from_form service method, suggested-name endpoint, is_system copy-from-source fix, secret carry-over without double-encryption).

key_reasoning.reason: Router (mcp_config.py), service (mcp_config_service.py new clone_from_form + request model), and clone_naming.py reuse span 2 layers; bumped because the new method reuses core shared helpers (_prepare_auth_config_for_persistence, _validate_auth_config_for_save, _ensure_auth_config_id) used by create/update, so a mistake here risks regressing those paths.

Task framing of today's is_system/is_public behavior is factually wrong per the analysis (is_system is hardcoded False, not forced True), the shape of the clone-request model (new field on create vs separate model) is an open design decision, and the non-oauth2/SAML carry-over question is an unresolved external verification gap (codemie-enterprise not inspectable).

The mask-and-carry-over mechanism (_prepare_auth_config_for_persistence with existing_encrypted_secret) is an established pattern from update, but applying it cross-record (source secret -> new row) is new ground with no existing test coverage, and getting it wrong double-encrypts a confidential client_secret, which is a security-sensitive, hard-to-detect regression.
